summary: The Monday arXiv window is strongest on STAR BES-II fluctuation and bulk-observable updates, BESIII transferable event representations, and practical statistical or scientific-ML methods that could transfer to HEP and nuclear-physics workflows. Heavy-ion-specific new material is mostly proceedings-level or idealized theory; the more actionable methodological contributions are low-yield discovery-significance formulae, pretrained event representations, sparse-observation PDE discovery, and learned kinetic closures.
strongest_paper: 2607.29088: Learning transferable event representations for charmed baryon physics at BESIII
top_takeaway: The most directly useful new physics-AI/ML item is the BESIII Particle-Transformer pretraining study; the most directly heavy-ion-relevant item is the STAR BES-II proceedings synthesis, which is scientifically important but not a full new analysis paper.

papers.title: Recent STAR Measurements from the RHIC Beam Energy Scan II
papers.authors_short: Ashish Pandav for the STAR Collaboration
papers.abstract: The proceedings contribution summarizes selected STAR BES-II results from collider and fixed-target running over sqrt(sNN)=3.0--27 GeV, plus isobar results at 200 GeV. The covered observables include bulk properties, strangeness production, femtoscopy, collectivity, hyperon polarization, and fluctuation observables relevant to QCD phase-structure searches.

papers.title: Weak Bose-Einstein condensation in a rigidly rotating magnetized charged Bose gas
papers.abstract: The paper studies an idealized noninteracting charged Bose gas under strong magnetic field and rigid rotation using finite-temperature field theory and generalized Fock-Schwinger methods. It argues that rotation modifies magnetic response and is more pronounced under parameter choices relevant to QGP than neutron-star matter, while not qualitatively changing weak BEC from Landau quantization.

papers.title: Learning transferable event representations for charmed baryon physics at BESIII
papers.authors_short: Kaixuan Huang, Yangu Li, Junpeng Zhao, Peilian Li, Peirong Li, Xiaorui Lyu, Yunxuan Song, Shengsen Sun, Yangheng Zheng
papers.abstract: A Particle Transformer framework is pretrained on BESIII Monte Carlo samples for event classification and momentum-direction regression, then fine-tuned across Lambda_c+ decay channels. The abstract reports 97.0% background rejection at 90.0% signal efficiency and consistent gains in low-statistics regimes across 12 benchmark decay channels.

papers.title: Discovery Sensitivity for a Counting Experiment with Background Uncertainty
papers.abstract: The paper derives approximate median discovery-significance formulae for Poisson counting experiments with known or control-region-constrained background. It uses profile-likelihood Asimov formulae plus Barndorff-Nielsen higher-order corrections and validates them against Monte Carlo and common particle-physics approximations.

papers.title: Freeze, Then Select: Structured Field Adapters and Stability-Validated Weak Selection for PDE Discovery from Sparse Observations
papers.authors_short: Juncheng Zhong, Chenghuang Shen, Jianfeng Liu, Zhengdong Xiao, Longjiu Luo, Qianrong Wang, Wenjun Xu, Wenlian Lu
papers.abstract: The method decouples sparse field reconstruction from equation selection by training a structured field adapter without a PDE residual, freezing the field, and selecting recurrent terms through stability-validated weak-form systems. It reports the best exact-support recovery across six sparse MDBench regimes and strong gains on Kuramoto-Sivashinsky dynamics.

papers.title: A Neural Operator Closure for Landau Damping in Electrostatic Plasma
papers.authors_short: Samuel Burles, Enrico Camporeale, Oreste Pezzi
papers.abstract: A Fourier Neural Operator is trained online inside a differentiable fluid solver to provide a non-Markovian closure for linear and nonlinear one-dimensional electrostatic Landau damping. The closure acts on a trailing window of resolved moments and remains stable in independent simulations, though the learned flux is expected to depend on the numerical scheme and training data.

papers.title: The fundamental limit of jet tagging: Beyond top jets
papers.abstract: This ACAT proceedings note extends likelihood-ratio-based studies of jet-tagger performance limits from boosted top jets to W, Z, and H->gg jets using transformer-based generative models with known densities. It reports that the gap between modern taggers and the estimated optimal limit is strongly jet dependent and smaller for some difficult tagging tasks.

cautions.title: MOT-SR: Multi-Objective Tool-Augmented Scientific Equation Discovery with Large Language Models
cautions.authors_short: Boxiao Wang, Runxiang Wang, Kai Li, Chongming Li, Zhiwei Chen, Yifan Zhang, Jian Cheng
cautions.abstract: The paper proposes an LLM-assisted multi-objective symbolic-regression loop with external analysis tools, Pareto optimization over accuracy/complexity/generalization, and a gravitational-wave EMRI validation case. It reports gains across 40 standard tasks, but the HEP/heavy-ion transfer path is indirect and the strength depends heavily on baseline fairness, prompt/tool robustness, and reproducibility of the closed-loop search.
